phase: calibration — supersession audit on real recorded revisions

corpus.source: merge tombstones (status: merged) — supersessions the graph already recorded

excluded.aliases: 88 present; these are 'aka' search synonyms (BRO-1423), not merged-away entities. Deriving supersessions from them would be prose inference.
excluded.contradicts: 30 keys present, 1 non-empty; none carries a recorded resolution naming a superseding record.

corpus.writes_to_live_graph: none — all runs against a pinned detached worktree

check_taxonomy.note: Eleven of twelve checks are DETERMINISTIC: given a page each either fires or does not, with no threshold and no dependence on a sample, so a false-positive RATE is not the quantity that describes them. This is not a claim that they are correct — determinism only moves the failure mode from statistical noise to SPECIFICATION ERROR, and the remedy for that is review of the predicate, not a larger corpus.
deterministic: temporal_recorded_at — parses / not in the future
temporal_supersedes — is a list / entries are strings / entries are [[wikilink]] form / not a self-reference
temporal_supersedes — target resolves to a live entity file
temporal_revision_link — present when supersedes is / non-blank / string / not an orphan
heuristic: temporal_supersedes / timeline inversion: the superseded target's recorded_at is newer than this record's
arguable_predicates: 'supersedes target resolves' — a target can be unresolvable because the tombstone was cleaned up, not because provenance is broken. Reporting it is a policy choice.
'recorded_at is in the future' — reads system time from the AUDIT HOST, so clock skew or cross-time-zone editing produces findings about the auditor rather than the record.
check_taxonomy.what_positive_controls_establish: REACHABILITY — each branch can fire, and fires on its own message. That is what makes a zero-finding corpus meaningful. It does NOT establish that firing was the right call.

positive_control.what: one injected defect per class, on a REAL migrated page; asserts the SPECIFIC field

power_limit.no_false_positive_rate_quoted: An earlier draft reported '0/7, 95% upper bound ~43%'. That has no coherent sampling unit: the corpus is 5 pages, 7 edges, and 0 heuristic-eligible comparisons at once, and a binomial bound requires one of those to be the trial. Removed rather than qualified.
power_limit.observed: zero envelope findings across every migrated canonical
power_limit.timeline_inversion_unexercised: timeline_inversion is NOT exercised by the real corpus: the check compares the superseded target's recorded_at, and merge tombstones do not carry one. Its probe above had to synthesise a stamp onto a tombstone. Calibrating it on real data would require the envelope on tombstones too — a design decision, not a measurement.

rationale: The 11 deterministic checks are reachable (12/12 positive controls, each matched on its own message) and silent on real data (0 findings across 5 migrated canonicals), and 7/7 mutations were killed. That is a soundness argument, not a precision measurement — and soundness is not a reason to gate NOW: only 5 of 943 pages can currently exhibit these fields, so a gate would have almost nothing to protect and no operational history behind it.
The 1 heuristic check (timeline inversion) is unmeasured on real data and cannot be measured on this corpus at all, because tombstones carry no recorded_at.
Everything stays warning-only and opt-in behind --temporal. Default lint is unchanged.
revisit_when: the envelope is present on a substantial share of the graph through ordinary merge/revise use (not a migration), giving the decidable checks something to protect;
tombstones carry recorded_at, which is what would make timeline inversion measurable on real data;
an independent reviewer has judged a set of real supersession findings.
